I am 70 years old, and I have farmed this land in Quzhou for half a century. I never went to school, but the land has been my teacher. My wife and I manage 13.1 mu together. We have a well, so water is reliable. I do not try new tricks—I plant what I know works. Every year, I split the land between winter wheat and summer maize. For wheat, I will sow improved seeds in mid-October after ploughing the field. I know wheat needs food, so I will put down compound fertilizer and top-dress with urea—altogether about 18 jin of nitrogen, 7 jin of phosphorus, and 5 jin of potassium per mu. I will irrigate four times: before sowing if the soil is dry, once before winter to protect the seedlings, once at jointing when the wheat shoots up, and once during grain filling. I will spray pesticide three times to control aphids and disease. I expect about 480 kg per mu if the weather cooperates. After harvesting wheat in early June, I will immediately sow hybrid maize. Maize grows fast and greedy, so I will give it 16 jin nitrogen, 6 jin phosphorus, and 4 jin potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times—after sowing, at the big trumpet stage, and during filling. Two pesticide sprays should handle the corn borer and weeds. I expect around 520 kg per mu. I use rotary tillage because it is easier on my old body than deep ploughing, and my small two-wheel tractor can handle it. At my age, I keep things simple: good seed, enough water, timely fertilizer, and watch the sky.
